caption: Cooking oil is poured into a pan over high heat, and the oil begins to shimmer and ripple across its surface.

sa.check: Oil is poured into a pan on a hob.
The oil's surface goes from still to moving.
Fine ripples run across the surface.
Thin wisps may rise from the oil.
The oil is still just after it is poured.
The pour comes first and the rippling follows.

pc.expect: The surface goes from still to rippling as the pan heats and the rippling keeps up.
pc.fail: The oil ripples while it is still falling from the bottle; or the surface goes glassy still and stays so while wisps rise from it; or the rippling stops and then starts again by itself; or the ripples appear before any oil is in the pan.

pc.expect: The ripples run across the oil's own surface and the oil stays in the pan; nothing else moves it.
pc.fail: The oil swirls as though stirred with nothing in the pan; or the whole body of oil slides from side to side in a still pan; or the pan shakes with nothing touching it; or the ripples hold one fixed pattern that never changes.

pc.expect: The oil lies level in the pan and finds its level as it is poured, and any wisps rise.
pc.fail: The oil's surface tilts and stays tilted with the pan level; or the oil climbs the pan's wall and stays above its level; or the wisps sink over the rim and pool on the hob; or the oil stands in a heap in the pan's middle.

pc.expect: The oil is a thin liquid that pours in a stream, spreads over the pan's floor and shows fine surface movement.
pc.fail: The oil pours as a solid rod; or the oil sets solid in the pan; or the oil moves as a single rigid sheet; or the oil beads up and rolls about without wetting the pan.

pc.expect: One pan and one pour; the oil stays in the pan and its level changes only by pouring.
pc.fail: The oil's level jumps up with nothing poured; or oil passes through the pan's wall; or a second pan appears; or the pan changes shape.

pc.expect: The pan, the hob and the oil's colour stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan changes colour; or the oil changes colour; or items around the hob rearrange.

note: Smoking of the oil is chemistry and is not judged.
